[00:00] Priya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm priya from redwood, quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: hi aisha here, leading ai at cobaltwell, excited to kick off.
[00:09] Marcus: marcus li, se, i'll be on the bench side and sizing.
[00:13] Tommy: tommy here, i'll handle infra questions.
[00:15] Dr. Lena: lena, clinical nlp lead.
[00:17] Markus: markus, cto. quick context from our side, we've got a backlog of clinical note processing across en/es/de, want automated extraction + routing with near real-time feedback.
[00:30] Priya: perfect. the call is to scope the poc — specifically success criteria (what counts as win), workload sizing (qps, concurrency, token distribution), bench plan and a shortlist of open models to try.
[00:45] Aisha: high level success: precision/recall for entity extraction > 0.88 on our holdout for EN/ES and >0.82 for DE, end-to-end latency under 600ms 95p for inline routing use case, and sustainable cost — ideally under $0.0009 per 1k tokens for inference when scaled.
[01:05] Dr. Lena: also need stability on clinical abbreviations and negation handling — those are the killers.
[01:12] Marcus: good, we'll factor those into the eval prompts. quick question on volume: tommy, what's current steady qps and peak?
[01:20] Tommy: steady ~7 qps, peak bursts to ~28 qps during clinic hours; avg note length ~350 tokens, but some long ones 2k tokens. we care mostly about 95p latency for short notes (~200 tokens) because routing needs to be fast.
[01:33] Priya: so a realistic bench should cover 1) short inferences (150–300 tokens) with concurrency up to 30 and 2) long-document extractions sampled at lower concurrency.
[01:45] Marcus: yes. i'll sketch GPU sizing for that distribution. rough numbers now: for a 13B-ish model quantized we expect ~150–250 tps (tokens/sec) per A100 equivalent for short context, but for 70B-quant on A100 maybe 350–500 tps with KV cache; these are rough — we'll confirm.
[02:05] Markus: which models are you thinking? we want open-models only for cost / licensing reasons.
[02:11] Priya: agreed. default shortlist for today: Llama-3-70B-quant (aggressive quant), Xenon-13B-multilang, Polyglot-7B-instruct, and MosaicMPT-30B-instruct. we also propose a smaller baseline like Polyglot-3B to measure latency/cost tradeoffs.
[02:30] Aisha: are those good on Spanish/Deutsch? we have legal docs in DE often.
[02:34] Marcus: polyglot & xenon were trained for multiple languages; xenon shows decent DE perf in our internal evals but tends to hallucinate on clinical jargon. 70B Llama-3 tends to be best quality but costs and GPU memory go up.
[02:50] Dr. Lena: hallucination is a showstopper. We need exact extraction of meds, dosages, and negation. Any mechanism to calibrate?
[02:58] Priya: yes — two levers: 1) use prompt engineering + constrained output schema (we can force structured JSON and use model scoring) and 2) run a reranker/verification model that checks extraction against the source text. Redwood supports function-like structured outputs and secondary rerankers in the pipeline.
[03:20] Tommy: latency impact? adding reranker adds extra calls.
[03:23] Marcus: can be done async or as a cheap 3B verification pass; for latency-critical path we can run the main model and a lightweight verifier in parallel and use the verifier to mark uncertain cases for human review. that'll add 40–120ms depending on model.
[03:40] Markus: okay. on infra, we prefer a VPC private deployment if possible because of PHI requirements. what are options?
[03:47] Priya: Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated reserved capacity with private networking. we can run the control plane managed or hand over. Both support KMS integrations and audit logs; we'll share SOC2/ISO docs.
[04:00] Aisha: great — send the security pack.
[04:03] Priya: noted. we'll attach to follow-up.
[04:08] [05:00] Marcus: going back to bench plan — propose three lanes: quality bench (holdout with metrics per language), latency bench (p95/99 under different concurrency and token lengths), and cost bench (tokens/sec * cost model). we'll instrument KV/prefix caching to see cache hit effects.
[05:25] Dr. Lena: for quality bench, we will provide 500 annotated notes per language (de-identified) — is that enough?
[05:33] Marcus: 500 each is a reasonable minimum for a POC. with that we can compute confidence intervals. also need a small set of edge cases (abbrev/negation) — maybe 100 across languages.
[05:45] Priya: timeline suggestion: share shortlist & benchmark template by 2/10; customer shares data by 2/11; SE runs initial bench 2/12–2/14; sync week of 2/15 with results & next steps.
[05:58] Markus: that timeline aligns with our internal sprint.
[06:02] Tommy: question on model variants — what about quantization options and mixed precision?
[06:07] Marcus: we'll try 8-bit & 4-bit quant profiles. Redwood's runtime supports int8/4 kernels and we can measure quality loss per profile. sometimes 4-bit introduces subtle quality drop on rare tokens — we'll include that in the quality bench.
[06:24] Aisha: any recommendations to start with? where do most customers land?
[06:27] Priya: many customers start with a mid-sized multilang model (13B) to balance cost and latency, then run a higher-quality 70B as a comparison. Based on your latency targets (600ms p95), a 13B quantized model often fits hosted/dedicated stacks easier.
[06:45] Dr. Lena: about evaluation metrics — precision/recall for entities is fine. do you support span-level F1?
[06:50] Marcus: yes we'll compute span-level F1, exact-match for structured fields like medication name/dose, and also a calibration score for hallucination (we'll compute the proportion of extractions with no supporting span).
[07:05] Priya: also recommend running a human-in-the-loop threshold for cases with low verifier confidence. we'll show expected human workload given thresholds during the bench.
[07:15] Markus: cost estimate example? ballpark per 1M tokens for those models?
[07:19] Priya: very rough: Polyglot-3B quant might be ~ $60–$120 per 1M tokens on dedicated pricing, 13B quant ~$250–$450 per 1M, and 70B-quant could be $900–$1400 per 1M depending on reserved vs burst capacity. we'll provide precise numbers with reserved capacity options and a model of batching/caching effects.
[07:40] Tommy: we need to see the effect of prefix caching — many notes start with templated headers.
[07:45] Marcus: absolutely — bench will include cache-on and cache-off scenarios. caching can reduce token cost significantly for repeated prefixes, sometimes 20–60% depending on hit rate.
[07:58] Aisha: can Redwood route between models? e.g., cheap baseline for most, fall back to 70B when uncertain?
[08:04] Priya: yes — smart routing policies are supported. you can route by confidence, cost, or user-defined policy. we can demo a canary that sends low-confidence calls to the 70B.
[08:15] Dr. Lena: about languages — our German corpora has lots of technical terms and Latin abbreviations. should we consider fine-tuning?
[08:23] Marcus: if the baseline models underperform on DE, a small instruction-tuning or LoRA on relevant corpus often helps. for POC we can measure out-of-the-box performance first and then decide. fine-tune adds time and requires more data governance.
[08:38] Markus: data governance — storing training/fine-tune material — would that remain within our VPC?
[08:43] Priya: yes with Private deployment all data resides in your VPC and KMS. For Hosted we offer options for ephemeral caching and non-retention configs. we'll include a matrix in the security pack.
[08:58] [10:00] Tommy: what about throughput testing? do you have a runner?
[10:03] Marcus: Redwood provides a load runner that simulates token distributions and concurrency. we'll run multiple scenarios: steady state, bursty traffic, and long-doc bursts to measure memory pressure. results will include GPU utilization and per-token latency distributions.
[10:20] Aisha: fantastic. do you have any suggested prompts or prompt templates for clinical extraction?
[10:25] Priya: yes, we'll include templates and structured-output examples — think explicit field lists, examples with negation and abbreviation. we'll also propose a verification prompt for the verifier model.
[10:35] Dr. Lena: for the quality bench, can you output span indices so we can map back to raw note?
[10:40] Marcus: yes we can return span offsets; just note tooling differences in tokenization across models — we'll normalize.
[10:48] Aisha: can we do a small pilot with Polyglot-7B first to show quick wins?
[10:52] Priya: absolutely — suggest a two-track POC: fast-track (Polyglot-7B baseline, 1 week) and deep-track (13B/70B comparative bench, 1–2 weeks).
[11:04] Markus: that helps our stakeholders. any blockers?
[11:07] Tommy: only needing to sanitize and export the notes in time.
